_comment: Utterance templates for the MOCK tutor only. The real Call 2 replaces this
entirely (server/llm.py, week 2). Kept out of Python so the mock obeys the
no-hard-coding rule and so Person B can reword the demo script without
Placeholders: {labels} = comma-joined focus node labels, {first} = first
focus label, {n} = number of nodes still lit.
Templates are indexed by hint_level, clamped to the list length.
RULE FOR EDITING: never write a literal count ('two left') - use {n}. A
template that states a number the graph contradicts is exactly the kind of
text/visual mismatch this project exists to avoid, and it would show up on
RULE FOR EDITING: hint_visual must never name the answer. It points at the
screen; that is the whole thesis.

BACKTRACK CARRIES NO NAME. Under CALL2_FIDELITY (server/turn.py) backtrack gets a lit COUNT and no identities, because start_item() has already moved to the target - so {first} would render the NEW item's answer. The graph moves the student; the text must not name where.

CONCLUDE IS THE CIRCUIT BREAKER'S LAST TURN. No item is open and none is coming, so it must not promise a next question. It also must not read as a failure notice: the tutor is choosing to stop, which is a different thing from the student running out.
ask: Have a look at the map. Which node fits?
Take another look at what's lit up. Which one is it?
hint_visual: I've dimmed everything that can't be it - {n} left.
Narrowing further: {n} candidates. Look at what they have in common.
Down to {n}. One of these is the answer.
{n} left. Which of them comes first?
It's one of the {n} still lit.
hint_verbal: Think about what has to be true before this step can happen.
Consider what the sender knows about the network at that moment.
It's the phase that runs before the next one takes over.
Think about which of these the others are built on.
backtrack: This one leans on something earlier. Let's go back and shore that up first.
Before we continue, there's a step underneath this that needs to be solid.
explain: Here's {first} in short - read it, then we'll come back to the question.
Short version of {first}, then we'll retry.
resolved_with_support: We've spent enough turns here - it's {first}. Let's move on and come back to it later.
conclude: Let's stop here for today. The ideas that stayed hard are the ones worth coming back to fresh.
Good place to leave it. We'll pick up the parts that fought back next time.
complete: That's the whole map. Every node on it is one you placed yourself.
Done - the map is covered. Worth a look back at the shape of it before you go.
